section_1.title: Prerequisite: Scalar vs. Vector
section_1.content: Differentiate between values that only have size (scalars) and values that have both size and direction (vectors). Establish the visual language: a dot vs. an arrow.
section_1.example: An ant is walking. If we say it moves at 2 cm/s, that is a 'Scalar' (Speed). If we say it moves 2 cm/s 'Right', that is a 'Vector' (Velocity).

section_2.title: The Visual Vector: Magnitude and Direction
section_2.content: Introduce the geometric representation of a vector as an arrow on a 2D coordinate grid. Define 'Magnitude' as the length and 'Direction' as the angle.
section_2.example: Imagine a drone flying from the origin (0,0) to a point (3,4). We draw an arrow pointing there. The length of this arrow represents the drone's power, and the tilt shows its flight path.

section_3.title: The Algebraic Vector: Coordinates
section_3.content: Translate the visual arrow into a list of numbers (components). Show how the vector [x, y] represents 'steps' taken along the axes.
section_3.example: The drone's flight vector is written as v = [3, 4]. This means 'move 3 units right and 4 units up'. This numerical pair allows computers to understand the arrow's 'shape'.

section_4.title: Vector Scaling: The Growth Potion
section_4.content: Explain Scalar Multiplication. Show how multiplying a vector by a number (scalar) stretches, shrinks, or reverses the arrow without changing its basic line of action.
section_4.example: If our drone vector is v = [3, 4], and we double its speed (2v), the arrow becomes twice as long: [6, 8]. If we multiply by -1, the drone flies in the exact opposite direction.

section_5.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
section_5.content: Demonstrate how to combine two vectors visually and mathematically. Use the 'Head-to-Tail' method to show the resulting 'Net' movement.
section_5.example: A boat tries to cross a river. Vector A is the boat's engine pointing forward. Vector B is the water current pushing sideways. Place the tail of B at the tip of A; the 'Resultant' vector shows where the boat actually ends up.

section_6.title: Application: Vectors in the Real World
section_6.content: Summarize how these basics form the foundation of Linear Algebra and their use in modern technology like video games and AI.
section_6.example: In a video game, every character's movement, the force of a jump, and even the direction of light hitting a wall are calculated using these exact vector additions and scaling rules.

outline.content: Demonstrate how to combine two vectors visually and mathematically. Use the 'Head-to-Tail' method to show the resulting 'Net' movement.
outline.example: A boat tries to cross a river. Vector A is the boat's engine pointing forward. Vector B is the water current pushing sideways. Place the tail of B at the tip of A; the 'Resultant' vector shows where the boat actually ends up.

storyboard.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
lecture_lines: Combining movements is called vector addition.
Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.
The result connects the start to the end.
This new arrow is the resultant vector.
It shows the total net movement.
animations: Draw a deep sky blue arrow (#00BFFF) labeled "Vector A" pointing up.
Draw a yellow arrow (#FFFF00) labeled "Vector B" pointing right.
Shift the yellow arrow (#FFFF00) so its tail touches the tip of Vector A.
Draw a magenta arrow (#FF00FF) from the start of A to the end of B labeled "Resultant".
Flash the magenta arrow (#FF00FF) to highlight the final path.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Prerequisite: Scalar vs. Vector"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalars represent size or magnitude alone.",
            "Vectors include both magnitude and direction.",
            "Think of a dot versus an arrow."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a white dot (#FFFFFF) labeled "Scalar: 2 cm/s".
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        scalar_label = Text("Scalar: 2 cm/s", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(scalar_label, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Write(scalar_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the dot into a green arrow (#00FF00) pointing right labeled "Vector: 2 cm/s Right".
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vector_label = Text("Vector: 2 cm/s Right", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(vector_label, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(dot, arrow),
            ReplacementTransform(scalar_label, vector_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Scale the green arrow (#00FF00) to double its length to show increased magnitude.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # We update the label too for context
        magnitude_label = Text("Magnitude increases", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(magnitude_label, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            arrow.animate.scale(2),
            FadeIn(magnitude_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule",
            [
                "Combining movements is called vector addition.",
                "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.",
                "The result connects the start to the end.",
                "This new arrow is the resultant vector.",
                "It shows the total net movement."
            ]
        )

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_A = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        COLOR_B = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_RESULTANT = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Combining movements is called vector addition."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Draw Vector A pointing up from D2 to B2
        vec_a = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B2"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{A}", color=COLOR_A, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C1") # Position label near Vector A

        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Draw Vector B initially pointing right from D2 to D4
        vec_b = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["D4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_B,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{B}", color=COLOR_B, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "E3") # Position label near Vector B's initial location

        self.play(Create(vec_b), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Shift Vector B so its tail is at Vector A's tip (B2)
        # We'll use a ValueTracker to animate the shift smoothly
        shift_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Initial positions
        b_start_init = self.grid["D2"]
        b_end_init = self.grid["D4"]
        label_b_init = self.grid["E3"]
        
        # Final positions
        b_start_final = self.grid["B2"]
        b_end_final = self.grid["B4"]
        label_b_final = self.grid["A3"]

        def update_vec_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_start = (1 - alpha) * b_start_init + alpha * b_start_final
            new_end = (1 - alpha) * b_end_init + alpha * b_end_final
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(new_start, new_end)

        def update_label_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_pos = (1 - alpha) * label_b_init + alpha * label_b_final
            mob.move_to(new_pos)

        vec_b.add_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.add_updater(update_label_b)
        
        self.play(shift_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        vec_b.remove_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.remove_updater(update_label_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The result connects the start to the end."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        # Resultant vector from start of A (D2) to end of B (B4)
        vec_res = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_RESULTANT,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        self.play(Create(vec_res))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "This new arrow is the resultant vector."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        label_res = Text("Resultant", color=COLOR_RESULTANT, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_res, "C5", scale_factor=0.8) # Label near the resultant
        
        self.play(Write(label_res))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "It shows the total net movement."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        # Flash the resultant vector to highlight it
        self.play(Flash(vec_res, color=COLOR_RESULTANT, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(vec_res, color=COLOR_RESULTANT))
        self.wait(2)

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule",
            [
                "Combining movements is called vector addition.",
                "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.",
                "The result connects the start to the end.",
                "This new arrow is the resultant vector.",
                "It shows the total net movement."
            ]
        )

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_A = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        COLOR_B = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_RESULTANT = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Combining movements is called vector addition."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Draw Vector A pointing up from D2 to B2
        vec_a = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B2"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{A}", color=COLOR_A, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C1") # Position label near Vector A

        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Draw Vector B initially pointing right from D2 to D4
        vec_b = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["D4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_B,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{B}", color=COLOR_B, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "E3") # Position label near Vector B's initial location

        self.play(Create(vec_b), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Shift Vector B so its tail is at Vector A's tip (B2)
        shift_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Initial positions
        b_start_init = self.grid["D2"]
        b_end_init = self.grid["D4"]
        label_b_init = self.grid["E3"]
        
        # Final positions
        b_start_final = self.grid["B2"]
        b_end_final = self.grid["B4"]
        label_b_final = self.grid["A3"]

        def update_vec_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_start = (1 - alpha) * b_start_init + alpha * b_start_final
            new_end = (1 - alpha) * b_end_init + alpha * b_end_final

            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_pos = (1 - alpha) * label_b_init + alpha * label_b_final
            mob.move_to(new_pos)

        label_b.add_updater(update_label_b)

        vec_b.remove_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.remove_updater(update_label_b)

            end=self.grid["B4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_RESULTANT,

            "- Direction is the angle of the path."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_ARROW = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GRID = "#444444"
        COLOR_ORIGIN = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_MAGNITUDE = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_DIRECTION = "#FF4500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        # Draw the background grid manually using grid positions
        grid_group = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]:
            grid_group.add(Line(self.grid[f"{r}1"], self.grid[f"{r}6"], color=COLOR_GRID, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
            grid_group.add(Line(self.grid[f"A{c}"], self.grid[f"F{c}"], color=COLOR_GRID, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        
        origin_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_ORIGIN, radius=0.08)
        self.place_at_grid(origin_dot, 'E2')
        
        # Vector v from origin E2 to A5 (3 units right, 4 units up)

        end_pos = self.grid['A5']
        vector_v = Arrow(start=start_pos, end=end_pos, color=COLOR_ARROW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        label_v = MathTex("\\vec{v}", color=COLOR_ARROW)
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_v), Write(label_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Magnitude is the arrow's physical length."
        
        # Define offset points for the brace to represent magnitude
        # Direction: (3, 4). Normal: (-4, 3). Normalized offset: (-0.4, 0.3)
        normal_offset = np.array([-0.4, 0.3, 0])
        brace_start = start_pos + normal_offset
        brace_end = end_pos + normal_offset
        
        magnitude_brace = BraceBetweenPoints(brace_end, brace_start, color=COLOR_MAGNITUDE)
        label_magnitude = Text("Magnitude", color=COLOR_MAGNITUDE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_magnitude, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_MAGNITUDE))
        self.play(Create(magnitude_brace), FadeIn(label_magnitude))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Direction is the angle of the path."
        
        # Arc representing the angle at the origin
        angle_val = np.arctan2(4, 3)
        direction_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.7, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=angle_val, 
            arc_center=start_pos, 
            color=COLOR_DIRECTION
        )
        
        label_direction = Text("Direction", color=COLOR_DIRECTION, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_direction, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIRECTION))
        self.play(Create(direction_arc), FadeIn(label_direction))
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: Prerequisite: Scalar vs. Vector
section_1.content: Differentiate between values that only have size (scalars) and values that have both size and direction (vectors). Establish the visual language: a dot vs. an arrow.
section_1.example: An ant is walking. If we say it moves at 2 cm/s, that is a 'Scalar' (Speed). If we say it moves 2 cm/s 'Right', that is a 'Vector' (Velocity).

section_2.title: The Visual Vector: Magnitude and Direction
section_2.content: Introduce the geometric representation of a vector as an arrow on a 2D coordinate grid. Define 'Magnitude' as the length and 'Direction' as the angle.
section_2.example: Imagine a drone flying from the origin (0,0) to a point (3,4). We draw an arrow pointing there. The length of this arrow represents the drone's power, and the tilt shows its flight path.

section_3.title: The Algebraic Vector: Coordinates
section_3.content: Translate the visual arrow into a list of numbers (components). Show how the vector [x, y] represents 'steps' taken along the axes.
section_3.example: The drone's flight vector is written as v = [3, 4]. This means 'move 3 units right and 4 units up'. This numerical pair allows computers to understand the arrow's 'shape'.

section_4.title: Vector Scaling: The Growth Potion
section_4.content: Explain Scalar Multiplication. Show how multiplying a vector by a number (scalar) stretches, shrinks, or reverses the arrow without changing its basic line of action.
section_4.example: If our drone vector is v = [3, 4], and we double its speed (2v), the arrow becomes twice as long: [6, 8]. If we multiply by -1, the drone flies in the exact opposite direction.

section_5.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
section_5.content: Demonstrate how to combine two vectors visually and mathematically. Use the 'Head-to-Tail' method to show the resulting 'Net' movement.
section_5.example: A boat tries to cross a river. Vector A is the boat's engine pointing forward. Vector B is the water current pushing sideways. Place the tail of B at the tip of A; the 'Resultant' vector shows where the boat actually ends up.

section_6.title: Application: Vectors in the Real World
section_6.content: Summarize how these basics form the foundation of Linear Algebra and their use in modern technology like video games and AI.
section_6.example: In a video game, every character's movement, the force of a jump, and even the direction of light hitting a wall are calculated using these exact vector additions and scaling rules.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Prerequisite: Scalar vs. Vector"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Scalars represent size or magnitude alone.",
            "Vectors include both magnitude and direction.",
            "Think of a dot versus an arrow."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a white dot (#FFFFFF) labeled "Scalar: 2 cm/s".
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        scalar_label = Text("Scalar: 2 cm/s", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(scalar_label, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(dot),
            Write(scalar_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform the dot into a green arrow (#00FF00) pointing right labeled "Vector: 2 cm/s Right".
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FF00", buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        vector_label = Text("Vector: 2 cm/s Right", font_size=20, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(vector_label, "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(dot, arrow),
            ReplacementTransform(scalar_label, vector_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Scale the green arrow (#00FF00) to double its length to show increased magnitude.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # We update the label too for context
        magnitude_label = Text("Magnitude increases", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(magnitude_label, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            arrow.animate.scale(2),
            FadeIn(magnitude_label)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Visual Vector: Magnitude and Direction", [
            "- Visually, a vector is an arrow.",
            "- Magnitude is the arrow's physical length.",
            "- Direction is the angle of the path."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_ARROW = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GRID = "#444444"
        COLOR_ORIGIN = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_MAGNITUDE = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_DIRECTION = "#FF4500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Visually, a vector is an arrow."
        
        # Draw the background grid manually using grid positions
        grid_group = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]:
            grid_group.add(Line(self.grid[f"{r}1"], self.grid[f"{r}6"], color=COLOR_GRID, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
            grid_group.add(Line(self.grid[f"A{c}"], self.grid[f"F{c}"], color=COLOR_GRID, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        
        origin_dot = Dot(color=COLOR_ORIGIN, radius=0.08)
        self.place_at_grid(origin_dot, 'E2')
        
        # Vector v from origin E2 to A5 (3 units right, 4 units up)
        start_pos = self.grid['E2']
        end_pos = self.grid['A5']
        vector_v = Arrow(start=start_pos, end=end_pos, color=COLOR_ARROW, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        label_v = MathTex("\\vec{v}", color=COLOR_ARROW)
        self.place_at_grid(label_v, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_ARROW))
        self.play(Create(grid_group), FadeIn(origin_dot))
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector_v), Write(label_v))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Magnitude is the arrow's physical length."
        
        # Define offset points for the brace to represent magnitude
        # Direction: (3, 4). Normal: (-4, 3). Normalized offset: (-0.4, 0.3)
        normal_offset = np.array([-0.4, 0.3, 0])
        brace_start = start_pos + normal_offset
        brace_end = end_pos + normal_offset
        
        magnitude_brace = BraceBetweenPoints(brace_end, brace_start, color=COLOR_MAGNITUDE)
        label_magnitude = Text("Magnitude", color=COLOR_MAGNITUDE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_magnitude, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_MAGNITUDE))
        self.play(Create(magnitude_brace), FadeIn(label_magnitude))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Direction is the angle of the path."
        
        # Arc representing the angle at the origin
        angle_val = np.arctan2(4, 3)
        direction_arc = Arc(
            radius=0.7, 
            start_angle=0, 
            angle=angle_val, 
            arc_center=start_pos, 
            color=COLOR_DIRECTION
        )
        
        label_direction = Text("Direction", color=COLOR_DIRECTION, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_direction, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_DIRECTION))
        self.play(Create(direction_arc), FadeIn(label_direction))
        self.wait(2)

        lines = [
            "Scaling changes a vector's size.",
            "Multiplying by two doubles its length.",
            "Negative multipliers reverse the vector's direction."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the original light blue vector v = [3, 4] (#00FFFF).
        # We'll use D3 as the anchor origin for the vectors.
        origin = self.grid["D3"]

            Transform(label_v, label_neg_v)
        )

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule",
            [
                "Combining movements is called vector addition.",
                "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.",
                "The result connects the start to the end.",
                "This new arrow is the resultant vector.",
                "It shows the total net movement."
            ]
        )

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_A = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        COLOR_B = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_RESULTANT = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Combining movements is called vector addition."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Draw Vector A pointing up from D2 to B2
        vec_a = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B2"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{A}", color=COLOR_A, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C1") # Position label near Vector A

        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Draw Vector B initially pointing right from D2 to D4
        vec_b = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["D4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_B,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{B}", color=COLOR_B, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "E3") # Position label near Vector B's initial location

        self.play(Create(vec_b), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Shift Vector B so its tail is at Vector A's tip (B2)
        # We'll use a ValueTracker to animate the shift smoothly
        shift_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Initial positions
        b_start_init = self.grid["D2"]
        b_end_init = self.grid["D4"]
        label_b_init = self.grid["E3"]
        
        # Final positions
        b_start_final = self.grid["B2"]
        b_end_final = self.grid["B4"]
        label_b_final = self.grid["A3"]

        def update_vec_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_start = (1 - alpha) * b_start_init + alpha * b_start_final
            new_end = (1 - alpha) * b_end_init + alpha * b_end_final
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(new_start, new_end)

        def update_label_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_pos = (1 - alpha) * label_b_init + alpha * label_b_final
            mob.move_to(new_pos)

        vec_b.add_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.add_updater(update_label_b)
        
        self.play(shift_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        vec_b.remove_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.remove_updater(update_label_b)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The result connects the start to the end."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        # Resultant vector from start of A (D2) to end of B (B4)
        vec_res = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_RESULTANT,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        self.play(Create(vec_res))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "This new arrow is the resultant vector."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        label_res = Text("Resultant", color=COLOR_RESULTANT, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_res, "C5", scale_factor=0.8) # Label near the resultant
        
        self.play(Write(label_res))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "It shows the total net movement."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        # Flash the resultant vector to highlight it
        self.play(Flash(vec_res, color=COLOR_RESULTANT, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(vec_res, color=COLOR_RESULTANT))
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Application: Vectors in the Real World", [
            "Vectors are foundational to modern technology.",
            "Video games use them for movement and physics.",
            "Even AI relies on these simple mathematical arrows."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Vectors are foundational to modern technology.
        # Show a white dot (#FFFFFF) representing a character with a velocity vector.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        character = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(character, "D2")
        
        vel_start = self.grid["D2"]
        vel_end = self.grid["D4"]
        velocity_arrow = Arrow(vel_start, vel_end, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        vel_label = Text("Velocity", color=WHITE, font_size=16)
        self.place_at_grid(vel_label, "E3") # Below the vector

            Create(character), 
            Create(velocity_arrow), 
            Write(vel_label), 
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        # Add a gold force vector (#FFD700) labeled "Jump" pointing upwards.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

            run_time=1
        )

            Create(resultant_arrow), 
            Write(res_label), 
            run_time=1.5
        )

outline.title: Prerequisite: Scalar vs. Vector
outline.content: Differentiate between values that only have size (scalars) and values that have both size and direction (vectors). Establish the visual language: a dot vs. an arrow.
outline.example: An ant is walking. If we say it moves at 2 cm/s, that is a 'Scalar' (Speed). If we say it moves 2 cm/s 'Right', that is a 'Vector' (Velocity).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Scalar vs. Vector
lecture_lines: Scalars represent size or magnitude alone.
Vectors include both magnitude and direction.
Think of a dot versus an arrow.
animations: Display a white dot (#FFFFFF) labeled "Scalar: 2 cm/s".
Transform the dot into a green arrow (#00FF00) pointing right labeled "Vector: 2 cm/s Right".
Scale the green arrow (#00FF00) to double its length to show increased magnitude.

outline.example: If our drone vector is v = [3, 4], and we double its speed (2v), the arrow becomes twice as long: [6, 8]. If we multiply by -1, the drone flies in the exact opposite direction.

Negative multipliers reverse the vector's direction.

outline.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
outline.content: Demonstrate how to combine two vectors visually and mathematically. Use the 'Head-to-Tail' method to show the resulting 'Net' movement.
outline.example: A boat tries to cross a river. Vector A is the boat's engine pointing forward. Vector B is the water current pushing sideways. Place the tail of B at the tip of A; the 'Resultant' vector shows where the boat actually ends up.

storyboard.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
lecture_lines: Combining movements is called vector addition.
Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.
The result connects the start to the end.
This new arrow is the resultant vector.
It shows the total net movement.

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule",
            [
                "Combining movements is called vector addition.",
                "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.",
                "The result connects the start to the end.",
                "This new arrow is the resultant vector.",
                "It shows the total net movement."
            ]
        )

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_A = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        COLOR_B = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_RESULTANT = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Combining movements is called vector addition."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Draw Vector A pointing up from D2 to B2
        vec_a = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B2"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{A}", color=COLOR_A, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C1") # Position label near Vector A

        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Draw Vector B initially pointing right from D2 to D4
        vec_b = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["D4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_B,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{B}", color=COLOR_B, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "E3") # Position label near Vector B's initial location

        # Initial positions
        b_start_init = self.grid["D2"]
        b_end_init = self.grid["D4"]
        label_b_init = self.grid["E3"]
        
        # Final positions
        b_start_final = self.grid["B2"]
        b_end_final = self.grid["B4"]
        label_b_final = self.grid["A3"]

            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_start = (1 - alpha) * b_start_init + alpha * b_start_final
            new_end = (1 - alpha) * b_end_init + alpha * b_end_final
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(new_start, new_end)

            new_pos = (1 - alpha) * label_b_init + alpha * label_b_final
            mob.move_to(new_pos)

        label_b.add_updater(update_label_b)

        vec_b.remove_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.remove_updater(update_label_b)

            end=self.grid["B4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_RESULTANT,
            stroke_width=8
        )

        self.wait(1)

        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        label_res = Text("Resultant", color=COLOR_RESULTANT, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label_res, "C5", scale_factor=0.8) # Label near the resultant
        
        self.play(Write(label_res))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "It shows the total net movement."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        # Flash the resultant vector to highlight it
        self.play(Flash(vec_res, color=COLOR_RESULTANT, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(Indicate(vec_res, color=COLOR_RESULTANT))
        self.wait(2)

        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Visual Vector: Magnitude and Direction", [
            "- Visually, a vector is an arrow.",
            "- Magnitude is the arrow's physical length.",
            "- Direction is the angle of the path."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_ARROW = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GRID = "#444444"
        COLOR_ORIGIN = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_MAGNITUDE = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_DIRECTION = "#FF4500"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Visually, a vector is an arrow."
        
        # Draw the background grid manually using grid positions
        grid_group = VGroup()
        for r in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]:
            grid_group.add(Line(self.grid[f"{r}1"], self.grid[f"{r}6"], color=COLOR_GRID, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))
        for c in ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]:
            grid_group.add(Line(self.grid[f"A{c}"], self.grid[f"F{c}"], color=COLOR_GRID, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.5))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule",
            [
                "Combining movements is called vector addition.",
                "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip.",
                "The result connects the start to the end.",
                "This new arrow is the resultant vector.",
                "It shows the total net movement."
            ]
        )

        # Define Colors
        COLOR_A = "#00BFFF"  # Deep Sky Blue
        COLOR_B = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        COLOR_RESULTANT = "#FF00FF"  # Magenta

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Combining movements is called vector addition."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Draw Vector A pointing up from D2 to B2
        vec_a = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B2"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_A,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{A}", color=COLOR_A, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "C2") # Position label near Vector A (Issue 39 fix)

        self.play(Create(vec_a), Write(label_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Place the second vector's tail at the first tip."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Draw Vector B initially pointing right from D2 to D4
        vec_b = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["D4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_B,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{B}", color=COLOR_B, font_size=32)
        # Position label near Vector B's initial location (Issue 40 fix requested A4, but initial was E3)
        # Note: If we use A4 initially, the animation logic below needs to move it to its final position correctly.
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "A4")

        movement_icon.set_color(WHITE).scale(0.3)
        # Place icon near the tail of Vector B initially
        movement_icon.move_to(self.grid["D2"] + DOWN * 0.3)

        self.play(Create(vec_b), Write(label_b), FadeIn(movement_icon))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Shift Vector B so its tail is at Vector A's tip (B2)
        # We'll use a ValueTracker to animate the shift smoothly
        shift_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Initial positions (adjusted to match current placement)
        b_start_init = self.grid["D2"]
        b_end_init = self.grid["D4"]
        label_b_init = self.grid["A4"] 
        icon_init = movement_icon.get_center()
        
        # Final positions
        b_start_final = self.grid["B2"]
        b_end_final = self.grid["B4"]
        label_b_final = self.grid["A3"] # Keep final label B near the new position
        icon_final = self.grid["B2"] + DOWN * 0.3

        def update_vec_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_start = (1 - alpha) * b_start_init + alpha * b_start_final
            new_end = (1 - alpha) * b_end_init + alpha * b_end_final
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(new_start, new_end)

        def update_label_b(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_pos = (1 - alpha) * label_b_init + alpha * label_b_final
            mob.move_to(new_pos)
            
        def update_icon(mob):
            alpha = shift_tracker.get_value()
            new_pos = (1 - alpha) * icon_init + alpha * icon_final
            mob.move_to(new_pos)

        vec_b.add_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.add_updater(update_label_b)
        movement_icon.add_updater(update_icon)
        
        self.play(shift_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        
        vec_b.remove_updater(update_vec_b)
        label_b.remove_updater(update_label_b)
        movement_icon.remove_updater(update_icon)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(movement_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "The result connects the start to the end."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_RESULTANT))
        
        # Resultant vector from start of A (D2) to end of B (B4)
        vec_res = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["D2"],
            end=self.grid["B4"],
            buff=0,
            color=COLOR_RESULTANT,
            stroke_width=8
        )
        self.play(Create(vec_res))

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
